text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Speaking last night in Jakarta at a banquet hosted by Indonesia's President Soeharto, Prime Minister John Howard rejected one of the main pinnacles of Australia's trade policy, revealing he did not see Australia as a bridge between Asia and the West. Page3.

Exiled Tibetan spiritual leader the Dalai Lama said yesterday he was still keen to meet Prime Minister John Howard, but he said he understood that Australia would not wish to risk its relationship with China, which he described as a major power that was determined to demonstrate its independence. Page 3.

As the Federal Government seeks to bolster market sentiment in the lead-up to the partial sale of national telecommunications carrier Telstra, it is expected to announce changes to the Telstra board soon. The board currently has three vacancies with a furher five directors scheduled to leave in December. Page 5.

Australian food exporters are coming under more pressure, largely from Malaysia - Australia's third largest dairy market, accounting for A$150 million of exports - to ensure their products comply with Islamic requirements as signals grow stronger that halal-certification may eventually become a condition of importing any food to key Muslim markets. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Prime Minister John Howard, who arrived in Jakarta yesterday to a ceremonial welcome at the presidential palace on his first overseas tour as Prime Minister, renewed last night the fundamental importance of Australia's bilateral relationship with Indonesia, saying it was based on a shared commitment to each country's well being. Page 1.

As the Australian Broadcasting Corporation struggles to come to grips with a large budget black hole and a A$65 million budget cut, newly-appointed ABC chairman Donald McDonald yesterday called for commercial partners to support the national broadcaster's loss-making Australia television satellite service to the Asia Pacific region to avoid a possible Federal Government sale. Page 1.

The Federal Government last night noted the reports of Chinese disapproval of exiled Tibetan spiritual leader the Dalai Lama's visit to Australia, after a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman yesterday warned of possible retaliation over a meeting between the Dalai Lama and Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer. Page 1.

In a test case expected to trigger a flood of similar actions, a 44-year-old woman, who claims she was forced to give her baby son up for adoption when she was 16, is suing the New South Wales Government. Public Interest Advocacy Centre solicitor Bill McMnus said this is an important test case because there are potentially hundreds of women in Australia in a similar situation. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In a wide-ranging submission to the New South Wales Government's Higher School Certificate review, the heads of the State's top private schools, including Sydney Grammar, Cranbrook, Pymble Ladies' College and Ascham, have called for massive HSC reform and urged the Carr Government to abandon the Tertiary Entrance Rank as a means of measuring a student's performance in the HSC. Page 1.

In a cautious foray onto the world stage, Prime Minister John Howard yesterday commenced his first major overseas visit when he was formally welcomed to Indonesia by President Soeharto. Howard hopes the visit will help define Australia's complex relationsip with its giant neighbour. Page 1.

A 22-year-old unemployed man from Rushcutters Bay was remanded in custody overnight at the Bondi police station and will appear in the Waverley Court today, charged with the murder of British tourist Brian Hagland at Bondi 10 days go. Page 1.

Controversy continues to rage over New South Wales hospitals as State Health Minister Andrew Refshauge yesterday defended his record as minister, while still denying allegations made over the weekend about beds unused because of Budget cuts and deaths caued by long waiting lists. Refshauge will face his second no-confidence motion in three months when Parliament resumes today. Page 3.
THE AGE

The Victorian Opposition has questioned the political future of State Attorney-General Jan Wade, after strong criticism by several Supreme Court Judges accusing her of mismanaging her portfolio and casting doubts over her ability to fill the post as the chief law officer, because of fears she is neglecting her duty to defend the judiciary. Page A1.

Former Hawthorn football stars have been heckled and booed at the Camberwell Civic Centre, Melbourne, during a meeting which was organised as a forum for the exchange of views between the anti-merger group Operation Payback and the mainstream club supporters. Page A1.

Federal Health Minister Michael Wooldridge has ruled out the removal of the Medicare rebate for abortion as Tasmanian independent Senator Brian Harradine denied he was involved in any Telstra-related deals over the issue. Page A3.

Victoria is no longer the worst State for youth unemployment, despite joblessness of up to two per cent above the national average, according to studies by Adelaide University's social justice research foundation, which indicate a 19.5 per cent youth unemloyment rate compared to a 21.2 per cent figure in South Australia. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
